scope.space: O(n polylog n) bits for every fixed ε > 0
scope.output: Explicit matching edges, returned after the stream
scope.probability: All included algorithms are deterministic; the lower bound includes randomized constant-error algorithms.
scope.ratioDefinition: r = guaranteed |M| / OPT; larger is better
scope.quantifiers: At most two passes. The current algorithm guarantees 2 − √2 − ε for every fixed ε > 0; 2 − √2 is a limiting endpoint, not an attained guarantee of this theorem.
scope.exclusions: Bipartite-only upper bounds, random-order streams, three or more passes, weighted matching, value-only estimation, and larger memory budgets are different settings.

coverage: Six principal frontier milestones: five algorithms and the unconditional 8/9 barrier. Related endpoint-only, restricted-class and RS-parameterized results are retained separately.

results.title: On Graph Problems in a Semi-Streaming Model
results.sourceLocation: Section 3.1, p. 209 of the TCS 2005 journal version
results.statement: Greedy deterministically returns at least half of an optimum matching using one pass and O(n log n) bits; this is also valid with a two-pass budget.
results.notes: Classical baseline documented by this paper. No second pass is needed.

results.title: Maximum Matching in Semi-Streaming with Few Passes
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 6 and Algorithm 10; arXiv version 3, April 10, 2014
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass semi-streaming algorithm guarantees |M| ≥ (1/2 + 1/140) OPT on any graph and any edge order.
results.notes: This general-graph result was added in the 2014 full version. The published APPROX 2012 precursor treats bipartite graphs. The source is an explicit-matching algorithm with O(n polylog n) bits; its separate random-order and bipartite algorithms are outside this row.

results.title: Maximum Matching in Two, Three, and a Few More Passes Over Graph Streams
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 5.5 and Algorithm 3; space bound in the introduction
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass algorithm guarantees |M| ≥ (1/2 + 1/32) OPT in general graphs, using O(n log n) bits.
results.notes: The stronger 1/2 + 1/16 guarantee in the same paper requires triangle-free inputs. This row uses the general-graph theorem. First arXiv submission: February 8, 2017.

results.title: Maximum Matching Sans Maximal Matching: A New Approach for Finding Maximum Matchings in the Data Stream Model
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass semi-streaming algorithm returns an explicit matching of size at least 7/13 of optimum in general graphs.
results.notes: The first pass uses components including triangles, rather than only a maximal matching. First arXiv submission: September 13, 2021; proceedings published September 15, 2022; later Algorithmica 2024 version.

results.title: Fully Dynamic Matching: (2 − √2)-Approximation in Polylog Update Time
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 2 and Algorithm 1, Section 4; proof concludes on p. 10
results.statement: For every fixed ε > 0, a deterministic two-pass algorithm outputs matching edges with |M| ≥ (2 − √2 − ε) OPT in general graphs.
results.notes: The plotted 2 − √2 endpoint is approached from below. The streaming algorithm stores O(n poly(1/ε)) edges, giving O(n poly(1/ε) log n) bits; it is deterministic, unlike the paper's separate dynamic value-estimation algorithm. First preprint: July 17, 2023; SODA publication: January 4, 2024.

results.title: An Unconditional Lower Bound for Two-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Maximum Matching Approximation
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 6.1 in coauthor Naidu’s thesis, Chapter 6, printed p. 112; proof on pp. 131–133
results.statement: For every fixed ε > 0, any constant-error randomized two-pass algorithm guaranteeing |M| ≥ (8/9 + ε) OPT needs n^{1+Ω(1/(log log n)²)} bits, already on bipartite graphs.
results.notes: This rules out every fixed ratio strictly above 8/9 in semi-streaming space, including on general graphs. It does not rule out equality at 8/9. The theorem says constant error; success probability at least 2/3 is covered.

relatedResults.title: Near-Quadratic Lower Bounds for Two-Pass Graph Streaming Algorithms
relatedResults.statement: Deciding whether an n-vertex bipartite graph has a perfect matching in two passes, with success probability at least 2/3, requires Ω(n² / 2^{Θ(√log n)}) bits.
relatedResults.notes: Consequently exact maximum-matching construction cannot use semi-streaming space. This is an endpoint result, not a fixed subunit approximation ceiling; show only a point at β=1 if included.

relatedResults.title: On Two-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Maximum Bipartite Matching
relatedResults.statement: A possibly randomized two-pass algorithm that only retains a greedy maximal matching after its first pass and achieves 2/3 + ε needs n^{1+Ω(1/log log n)} space.
relatedResults.notes: The first-pass restriction is essential. This is not an impossibility ceiling for arbitrary two-pass algorithms and must not shade the general-setting frontier.

relatedResults.title: A Two-Pass Lower Bound for Semi-Streaming Maximum Matching
relatedResults.statement: A two-pass semi-streaming algorithm with success probability at least 2/3 is constrained by the density of Ruzsa–Szemerédi graphs. Known constructions give a near-one, n-dependent barrier; stronger RS-density assumptions give a constant barrier.
relatedResults.notes: The paper gives 0.98 as an illustrative excluded ratio under RS(n)=n^{1−o(1)}. It is not an unconditional 0.98 threshold. The 2024 unconditional 8/9 ceiling is stronger even than this hypothetical case; retain this as history, not a current numerical frontier.
